text: For Temasek as shareholder, it plays the role of an advocate for good corporate practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, Temasek fosters an ethos of integrity, good governance and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It does not condone improper conduct and malfeasance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Temasek expects companies in its portfolio to abide by sound corporate governance and robust codes of conduct and ethics and to comply with all laws and regulations of jurisdictions in which they have investments or operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, just last week, Mr Lim Boon Heng, the Chairman of Temasek, reiterated his expectation of governance to the Chairs of major Temasek portfolio companies at the annual Temasek Chinese New Year lunch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Lim said, and I quote: "In markets where practices are questionable and compromising integrity is required to win business or contracts, we have to be very clear – there is a bright red line our companies should not cross….

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also entrusted with the responsibility of being the owners and guardians of the company’s reputation, and we must always live up to that trust".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, Temasek regularly monitors the strategy and performance of its portfolio companies and keeps abreast of industry developments that impact them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This informs how Temasek exchanges and shares views and perspectives with the boards and management of its portfolio companies, so as to better understand their strategies and operating environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, Temasek conducts regular roundtables or forums on topics of interest to the portfolio companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Temasek organises or sponsors forums on topical issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include topics, such as cybersecurity, insider trading and corporate contributions to community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of these forums are also open to other companies in Singapore outside of Temasek's portfolio, as part of Temasek’s contributions to support good governance and sound stewardship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Changes or new legislation against corruption, such the Bribery Act in the United Kingdom (UK) and the laws on corrupt practices in the United States (US) and Singapore are covered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Other topics include corporate and functional aspects, such as legal, finance, HR or IT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These would be roundtables or forums for the practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Temasek is organising a roundtable on governance and ethics with its portfolio companies in the coming months, on norms and practices on ethical business operations and expectations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through these forums, Temasek actively encourages certain key practices, such as long-term incentives contingent on performance, or the institutionalisation of formal code of conduct or code of ethics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I move on now to the topic of tax deductions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Two other Members of Parliament (MPs) have spoken on this issue in recent months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee has also made representations to IRAS on behalf of the Association.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is in line with our long-standing national car-lite policy, as tax deduction of expenses incurred for a private car is not allowed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to monitor changes in business models and consumer habits in this area and will review our policies to ensure they remain relevant and effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Azmoon Ahmad spoke about tax deductions for donations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Extending the 250% tax deduction for donations is one of our efforts to encourage the spirit of giving in our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Tax deduction for both corporate and individual donations in Hong Kong, the US and Australia are at 100%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At 250% tax deduction rate, the Government co-funds 42.5 cents for every dollar donated by companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, the Government co-funds up to 55 cents for every $1 donated by individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A flat tax deduction rate, rather than a tiered tax deduction system suggested by Mr Azmoon Ahmad, ensures that donors who have the ability to donate more are not accorded exceptional tax treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many donors contribute out of passion and heart for the community, and not just for tax incentives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government continues to ensure fiscal prudence, create opportunities for our businesses and enhance citizen experience with technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have made good progress in these areas, and we will continue to improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are committed to work in partnership with our businesses, the community and citizens in this journey.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Surely, now that LTA recognises that vocation drivers for the private hire cars are fairly similar to taxi drivers, I think our tax deductible for car rental and fuel can be in keeping with the approach we do for taxi drivers for the Year of Assessment in this coming tax period.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I note Mr Ang's very passionate advocacy in this area.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I just want to echo what Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Henry Kwek have said about designs, how important design is when we look at building design, to make sure that it does not cost more to maintain thereafter.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, perhaps, can I ask the Minister whether, in the whole process, we should also seek inputs from Town Councils and NEA who will be there to maintain the building thereafter, to give inputs whether these designs are, indeed, practical?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: They may look very nice from afar, but is it practical to maintain on an ongoing basis?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The second point is on the issue of leverage, like what I have said in my speech, to leverage the private sector to achieve better value-for-money.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: For example, in my constituency, we have an Integrated Transport Hub (ITH), and next to it is a commercial shopping centre.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: If we could have in the planning requirements that require the developer to also build better connectivity to the ITH, for example, that would have saved us some money to build subsequent features to enhance walkability and connectivity.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, maybe this question is best directed at the Second Minister for Finance who is also the Minister for National Development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I am happy to take both questions in both capacities, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There will always be areas for improvement, I am sure, and we will continue to get feedback from all stakeholders, different agencies, Town Councils, different building users, so that we can continually improve.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this improvement is not, as I have said earlier, specific only to Government projects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are many other buildings that are being developed by the private sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we really have to get the whole architectural profession to start paying greater attention to designing for these purposes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On leveraging the private sector, we are in some ways already doing that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Member would realise we have made some adjustments to some of the requirements.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, it is an area which we will continue to improve.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, I have got three clarifications for the Senior Minister of State on the role of Temasek and also MOF.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier on, in her reply, the Senior Minister of State mentioned that Temasek was very active in promoting good governance, for example, by conducting seminars, training and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think that is more on a general level.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But she did not touch on whether Temasek had been active in, for example, querying suspicious practices in the companies that they invest in.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask her whether she is aware whether Temasek has been playing that role, specifically to query what has been going on in some of its portfolio companies.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is, in my speech as well as in her response, the Senior Minister of State did mention the Chinese New Year lunch sharing that the Chairman of Temasek had recently, where it was quite clear from his speech that corruption is an out of bound (OB) marker now specifically expressed as something that Temasek would not want to tolerate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is she aware of any other unethical practices that are OBs for Temasek?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For example, do they avoid investing in companies that promote unclean energy or promote tobacco, for example?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is she aware of any other OB markers for Temasek to invest in?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And, finally, the third clarification is: on the role of the Ministry itself, as the sole shareholder of Temasek, I think at least Mr Lim Boon Heng accepts that Temasek is flying Singapore's flag and, if anything were to happen that affects the reputation of its portfolio companies, our country's reputation would be affected as well.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether MOF actually has any specific parameters for Temasek as to certain things that should or would not be condoned as investments.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I understand, by comparison, the Norwegian Government has got certain excluded investments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chairman, if I may just take the last question first.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are a professional team and we expect them to live up to that expectation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in terms of the specific question whether we get involved in what they should invest in, what they should not invest in, the Government does not step into that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But our expectation is that Temasek must act properly and have good compliance with governance and the highest standards of integrity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And they, in turn, I think expect that, too, of their investee companies, as Members would have seen from the discussion that the Chairman had with its investee companies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Sylvia Lim's second question was where she said that corruption is now an OB marker.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It has been that case for a long time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the Member asked whether I was aware of specific investment principles.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will come back to what I said earlier, which is that, obviously, Temasek will not condone anything that is illegal, anything that is in breach of international regulations, basically anything that constitutes bad conduct or improper governance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think if one reads the speech given by Mr Lim Boon Heng to the investee companies, it really sets out or outlines what his expectation is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would not go through the whole thing but let me just give some excerpts where he said: "During my lunch remarks just now, I emphasised how important it is for our companies to guard and uphold the principles of good governance and integrity in business dealings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is especially so for our Singapore-based Temasek portfolio companies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore has a reputation as a clean place for both business and Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a hallmark of our nation and the fundamental value on which we have built our economy." He also went on to say: "We are stewards, responsible not just for short-term profits, but really the long-term future of our companies." And he called for their support to bring together all their board members, along with their CEOs and key executives, for their next Roundtable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I mean, in short, he is setting the guidance and direction for the portfolio companies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the third question was whether I was aware if Temasek is querying suspicious things.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think it really depends on what the scenario is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not have information on what Temasek's information on specific portfolio companies is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I think I can say this much with confidence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As shareholders, when you have your shareholders' meetings, obviously the audited accounts are placed before the shareholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would certainly expect Temasek, as a shareholder, if it sees anything in the accounts that look suspicious, to query it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Do I know or have any personal knowledge what their representatives do at their shareholders' meetings?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not, but does MOF expect Temasek, when it sees something suspicious in audited accounts, to raise it at shareholders' meetings?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Chairman, I just have one question for the Second Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This is with regard to the $4 billion that the Minister mentioned PUB was investing in for development purposes from the years 2017 to 2021 and that some of these requirements would actually be secured through borrowing which would, in the course of his explanation, explain the fact that Statutory Boards do actually borrow from the markets and they have a different approach vis-à-vis the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm how much will PUB be borrowing for this purpose, for this $4 billion that it needs to upgrade a number of transmission networks and so on?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The capital reserves are set aside and used for future investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And, indeed, when you look at future investment plans, PUB is committed to setting aside or investing $4 billion in additional water infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, obviously, some of this, besides coming out from its capital reserves, will need to be financed through borrowing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Exactly how much and when, I think that is something that PUB will have the information and they will reveal it in due course when they need to go to the markets.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the mover wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Is the hon Member given leave to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think leave of the majority is given, amendment is withdrawn.
